title: Modularize weight deserialization and decouple tokenizer bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We still carry a lot of implicit coupling between weight deserialization, shard placement, and tokenizer initialization. This causes three classes of problems: (1) slow cold-starts because the tokenizer and heavy deserialization run sequentially on the main load path, (2) fragile adapters when new weight formats are introduced, and (3) memory blowups when shard indices and tokenizer vocab mappings are retained longer than needed.

Goal:
Split the model load pipeline into clear, testable stages so we can: (a) stream weight bytes and build shard indices without forcing tokenizer binding to happen synchronously, (b) add a lightweight adapter registry for new/legacy weight formats, (c) introduce a lazy tokenizer bind step that only maps byte offsets to token ids when first used, and (d) reduce peak memory by releasing temporary buffers earlier. Target: reduce median cold-load latency by 20-30% for multi-shard models and cut peak working set during load by ~25%.

Design summary (high level):
- Stage 1: Header/manifest parse (synchronous, cheap). Produce a LoadPlan with shard descriptors and format tags.
- Stage 2: Shard index construction (streaming, IO-bound). Build a compact index of layer offsets, quantization metadata, and KV cache sizing. This stage writes metadata to an arena allocator that can be freed soon after runtime copies are made.
- Stage 3: Weight deserialization (parallel tasks per shard). Emit weight tensors into destination buffers. Use existing async IO and the new pool allocator to reduce GC churn.
- Stage 4: Tokenizer binding (lazy). Do not materialize tokenizer maps during Stage 2/3. Instead create a TokenizerBinder object that supports bind-on-first-token and has a deterministic fallback to legacy eager bind for older runtimes.
- Adapter registry: Implement a small registry (format -> adapter) that can be extended without touching the core loader. Include adapters for legacy zipped ckpt, flat-npy shards, and new streaming LZ4 blobs.

Compatibility and safety: 
- Provide a compatibility shim that runs legacy eager-bind behavior for deployments that set runtime flag `legacy_tokenizer_bind=true`. This facilitates incremental rollout.
- Add runtime checks to ensure that adapter reports complete layer coverage; reject partial adapters unless explicitly allowed by a migration flag.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for each pipeline stage and for adapter registry.
- Synthetic regression harness to compare weight->layer mapping between old and new loader for 50 representative models (small, mid, large).
- Perf microbenchmarks: cold-load median/95th, peak RSS during load, and time-to-first-inference.
- Add end-to-end smoke on Dedicated staging region for canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge adapter registry and header/manifest parsing (feature-flagged) — week 1.
2) Implement streaming shard index + pool allocator; run regression harness — week 2.
3) Add lazy tokenizer binder behind feature flag; run canary on ~5% of traffic for models with known good adapters — week 3.
4) Widen canary and finally flip flag once 7 days of stable metrics across cold-load and inference P99s.

Instrumentation and metrics to watch:
- loader.cold_load_ms (p50/p95), loader.peak_rss_mb, tokenizer.binds_per_min, adapter_errors_total, model.load_failures.

Open trade-offs / questions:
- Eager vs lazy tokenizer bind: lazy reduces peak but adds a potential first-token latency spike. We mitigate by pre-binding for hot models during warm pools.
- Pool allocator complexity vs benefit: initial measurement suggests ~15% reduction in allocation churn; if it regresses, we can revert the allocator and keep streaming index.

Migration notes for users/operators:
- No consumer-visible API changes to Redwood API. Internal model manifests will gain a `format` tag; ops tooling will surface warnings if a model uses a new/untested adapter.

Deliverables:
- loader: modular pipeline implementation behind feature flag (runtime-1.21).
- adapter registry + three adapters (legacy-zip, flat-npy, lz4-stream).
- regression harness and perf dashboards.
- runbook for rollback if load-failures > 0.5% over a 30-minute window during canary.
